coverage.why: All 17 venues resolved to a SeatGeek venue page and were read fully (no pagination encountered — each venue's tickets page appears to render its complete forward-looking event list in one load, no 'load more' control or page=2 links found in any page's markup). Four venues (empire, continental, summit, vulcan) have live, correctly-addressed SeatGeek pages that simply list no current events — this was verified with a second, independent fetch (raw links dump) for empire and continental to rule out an extraction miss. 'parish' and 'brushy' turned out to be the SAME SeatGeek venue page (SeatGeek's own page title acknowledges the real-world rename 'Brushy Street Commons (Formerly The Parish)') — both slugs carry identical events; see the per-event note. Two venue slugs (kingdom, summit) needed a keyword map-search rather than a guessed URL pattern to find the correct SeatGeek slug.

cityWide.note: Counted manually from the /cities/austin 'All Austin Events' feed, which SeatGeek renders as an infinite-scroll list starting from today (Sep 24, 2026) — only the first ~10 items load without further scroll/pagination interaction, all falling on Sep 23-24, 2026 (i.e. today and yesterday), so a true 'next 30 days' count could not be read from a single static fetch. The visible sample: Rise Against (Moody Amphitheater), Mrs. Doubtfire x2 (Bass Concert Hall), Geordie Greep (Mohawk), Rod Wave (Moody Center ATX), Rachel Scanlon + Joe Nunnink (Cap City Comedy Club, not one of our 17 venues), Jungle (Moody Center ATX), Adela (Emo's Austin), Freya Skye (Moody Amphitheater). Getting a real 30-day count would need either scroll-driven pagination (out of scope for a courtesy study) or a per-venue rollup from the events[] array above.

linkBehavior: Every event's 'url' field IS SeatGeek's own event/checkout page (e.g. https://seatgeek.com/dave-chappelle-tickets/comedy/2026-10-26-7-30-pm/18589333) — SeatGeek is itself the marketplace, so there is no separate outbound redirect to Ticketmaster/AXS/etc. visible from the venue listing page; 'ticketUrl' is recorded identically to 'url' for every event in this file. SeatGeek is a mixed primary+resale marketplace by design (it aggregates both the venue's own primary allotment and resale inventory on the same event page, often showing multiple price tiers like '1-3 tickets $X' which is a resale-marketplace tell) — determining primary-vs-resale per event would require opening each individual event page and reading its price-tier language, which was not done here to conserve the fetch budget (that would be ~330 additional fetches). This is recorded as a per-event caveat in 'notes' rather than guessed at. No outbound domain (ticketmaster.com, axs.com, etc.) was ever observed in the HTML — everything stays on seatgeek.com.
